summary: Argentina (update to arg-cbi): the Ministry of Economy announced on 2 Oct 2026 the prices of the citizenship-by-investment programme (USD 350,000 Treasury contribution or USD 800,000 programme bond; USD 100,000 per spouse/adult child, USD 25,000 per minor) and said it would open for applications in Q4 2026; no implementing resolution in the Boletín Oficial up to 9 Oct 2026, so status stays not_operational. Ethiopia: a 2026 Council of Ministers fee regulation (reported as No. 587/2026, in force 24 Feb 2026) created a property-linked five-year visa and residential ID for foreigners who buy property (USD 150,000 reported) and a 10-year 'Golden Visa' for investors of USD 5 million (later press: USD 10 million); known only from the press; the immigration agency's site has nothing on it. Guatemala: the Migration Code (Decreto 44-2016) gives temporary residence of up to five years to investors, and the IGM's Reglamento de Residencias Guatemaltecas (Acuerdo IGM-016-2025, signed 21 May 2025, approved by AMN 05-2025) sets the amount at USD 100,000 in companies or in movable or immovable property; after five years of temporary residence an investor can apply for permanent residence. No counts. Kazakhstan: an investor ('golden') visa leading to a residence permit of up to 10 years for USD 300,000 in charter capital of Kazakh companies or local securities, created by amending the investor-visa rules (Order No. 1265 of 29 Dec 2015) in spring 2025; only press sources could be read (adilet.zan.kz now needs credentials, gov.kz is script-rendered). Maldives: the Corporate Resident Visa is a real, gazetted residence-by-investment route (Regulation 2015/R-139 of 27 Apr 2015: USD 50 million investment, or USD 1 million deposited for 2 years, put in a financial security, or invested in approved real estate; replaced in substance by Regulation 2021/R-115 of 29 Aug 2021: USD 250,000 fixed deposit for 5 years or USD 250,000 in government-designated businesses, 5-year visa, MVR 15,000 fee). No counts found; the 2025-26 'Pearl Residence' programme is reported only in the press. Mauritius: a new Golden Visa Scheme (announced in Budget 2026/27; EDB guidelines of August 2026) gives a renewable two-year multi-entry visa to investors who undertake to invest USD 1 million in qualifying sectors within 12 months, after which they can apply for permanent residence; no processing fee. Not previously in the data. Rwanda: the 2021 Organic Law on nationality (in force 28 Jul 2021) allows nationality by acquisition on grounds of 'substantial sustainable investment', with a 2022 ministerial order listing the documents (proof of property, registration as an investor); no amount or price is set, so it is a discretionary investor route like Papua New Guinea's or Cabo Verde's. Uzbekistan: Presidential Decree PF-67 of 18 Apr 2025 (para. 26) gives a five-year residence permit, from 1 June 2025, for a payment of USD 250,000 plus USD 150,000 per family member, without buying property (the 'golden visa'); read in the official legislation database. No counts. Other candidates checked and not added are listed in gaps with the reason and the source relied on.

sources.title: Luis Caputo anunció la puesta en marcha del Programa de Ciudadanía por Inversión de Argentina
sources.covers: Announcement of the citizenship-by-investment programme: applications from Q4 2026; USD 350,000 non-refundable Treasury contribution or USD 800,000 programme bond; family contributions (USD 100,000 spouse/children 18-25; USD 25,000 under 18); family of four USD 500,000; vetting bodies and approval by the Dirección Nacional de Migraciones.
sources.notes: Official ministry news item; not a legal act. Amounts not yet in a resolution of the Ministry of Economy as of 9 Oct 2026 (Boletín Oficial, first section, scanned 30 Sep-9 Oct 2026).

sources.title: New Golden Visa Turns Residency Into a Bet on Foreign Capital
sources.covers: Press briefing by the Director General of the Immigration and Citizenship Service: property-based residential IDs and visas (property purchase, at least USD 150,000 reported), Golden Visa for USD 5 million investors (fee USD 10,000, 10 years), fee schedule of the revised Immigration & Citizenship Service Fee Regulation; ICS revenue for the first three quarters of the fiscal year.
sources.notes: The page carries no date; it reports ICS figures for 'the first three quarters of the fiscal year', which suggests spring 2026 (the Ethiopian fiscal year starts in July). Regulation number not given. Note the source_id has a year suffix (2026) inferred from that context.

sources.title: Ethiopia Overhauls Visa Framework to Attract Long-Term Investors
sources.author: Felix Tih
sources.covers: Immigration and Citizenship Service Fee Regulation No. 587/2026 (in force 24 Feb 2026): investment entry visa extended to 3 and 5 years, new 10-year multiple-entry Golden Visa; relays the Ethiopian Embassy in London's monthly 'The Brief'.
sources.notes: Page shows both 7 and 8 April 2026 as dates. Secondary report; the regulation itself (Negarit Gazette) was not found online.

sources.title: Código de Migración, Decreto Número 44-2016 del Congreso de la República de Guatemala
sources.publisher: Congreso de la República de Guatemala (copy published by the Instituto Guatemalteco de Migración)
sources.covers: Migration Code: art. 75(d) temporary residence for investors (up to five years); art. 78 permanent residence; art. 246 entry into force sixty days after publication in the Diario Oficial.
sources.notes: Issued by Congress 20 Sep 2016 and sanctioned 12 Oct 2016 (published_date is the sanction date); the Diario Oficial publication date is not printed in this copy, so the in-force date is not settled here.

sources.title: Reglamento de Residencias Guatemaltecas, Acuerdo No. IGM-016-2025 (aprobado mediante Acuerdo de Autoridad Migratoria Nacional No. AMN-05-2025)
sources.covers: Residence rules: art. 7 temporary residence 1-5 years, extendable; art. 17 investor temporary residence (USD 100,000 in commercial entities or in movable or immovable property); art. 18 extension; art. 27 permanent residence after five years of temporary residence (dependants of investors on proof the investment continues); art. 59 repeals Acuerdo IGM-092-2022; art. 60 in force as the National Migration Authority decides.
sources.notes: Signed by the IGM Director General on 21 May 2025 (published_date); the AMN approval (Acuerdo AMN-05-2025, named in the file name and on the IGM legislation page) and its in-force date are not in this copy. Listed on https://igm.gob.gt/index.php/nosotros/legislacion-igm.

sources.title: Kazakhstan Introduces Investor Visa in Bid for Foreign Investment
sources.covers: Foreign Ministry announcement (30 Apr 2025) of new investor visa rules: USD 300,000 in charter capital or listed local securities, residence permit up to 10 years, in force ten days after official publication.
sources.notes: Relays the Foreign Ministry press service; the decree or order is not named. Publication date from the URL month and the Google News listing (2 May 2025).

sources.title: Инвесторская виза: изменились условия получения
sources.covers: Summary of amendments to Order No. 1265 of the Minister for Investment and Development (29 Dec 2015) on the rules for issuing a petition for an investor visa: USD 300,000 invested in the last 12 months, petition issued for up to 10 years, residence permit up to 10 years, documents required.
sources.notes: Accounting news site; paraphrases the amended order but does not give the amending order's number or date. The order itself (adilet.zan.kz) could not be read: the site's API now requires credentials.

sources.title: ކޯޕަރޭޓް ރެސިޑެންޓް ވީޒާ ދޫކުރުމާބެހޭ ގަވާއިދު (Corporate Resident Visa Regulation), Regulation No. 2015/R-139, Dhivehi Sarukaarge Gazette Vol. 44 No. 176, 27 April 2015
sources.publisher: Department of Immigration and Emigration, Maldives (Government Gazette)
sources.covers: Founding regulation of the Corporate Resident Visa: qualifying investments (USD 50 million; USD 1 million bank deposit for 2 years or in a financial security; USD 1 million in ministry-approved real estate), family members covered, validity, USD 2,000 processing fee, entry into force on gazette publication (art. 13).
sources.notes: Gazette page https://www.gazette.gov.mv/gazette/3693. Dhivehi only. Text extracted with pdftotext in logical order; brackets in the extracted text are mirrored, quotes are given as printed.

sources.title: ކޯޕަރޭޓް ރެސިޑެންޓް ވީޒާ ދޫކުރުމާބެހޭ ގަވާއިދު (Corporate Resident Visa Regulation), Regulation No. 2021/R-115, Dhivehi Sarukaarge Gazette Vol. 50 No. 251, 29 August 2021
sources.publisher: Ministry of Economic Development, Maldives (Registrar of Businesses) (Government Gazette)
sources.covers: Reformed Corporate Resident Visa: three groups (shareholders, directors and senior staff of a registered foreign investment meeting company conditions; USD 250,000 fixed deposit for 5 years; USD 250,000 in government-designated businesses), family members, 5-year visa, renewal, cancellation, fee MVR 750 per 3 months (MVR 15,000 in total), quarterly publication of numbers issued (art. 21), entry into force on gazette publication (art. 22). Schedule 1 is an English application form.
sources.notes: Gazette page https://www.gazette.gov.mv/gazette/6200. Dhivehi with an English application form. The regulation does not say in the pages read that it repeals the 2015 regulation.

sources.title: Law No. 3/2025, Third Amendment to Law No. 1/2007 (Maldives Immigration Act), Dhivehi Sarukaarge Gazette Vol. 54 No. 66, 15 April 2025
sources.covers: Checked because it is the most recent amendment of the Immigration Act: it concerns entry on Israeli passports (art. 8), not investor residence. Nothing in scope.
sources.notes: Stored only to document that the 2025 amendment does not create an investor residence route.

sources.title: Golden Visa Scheme Mauritius: Guidelines (August 2026)
sources.covers: Overview, key features (visa up to 2 years, renewable, multi-entry, no processing fee, 5-working-day processing), conditions (written undertaking to invest USD 1 million within 12 months; bank statement showing USD 1 million), qualifying sectors, documents, application via NELS (EDB screens, Passport and Immigration Office issues), benefits (permanent residence after the investment; property purchase under IRS/RES/PDS/SCS), undertaking form, fast-track domestic worker permits.
sources.notes: Linked from the EDB info-centre page 'Golden Visa Scheme' (https://edbmauritius.org/info_centre/golden-visa-scheme, posted 24 Aug 2026). No legal instrument (regulation or Finance Act section) is cited in the guidelines.

sources.title: Golden Visa Scheme: Your Gateway to Residency (EDB Newsletter, August 2026)
sources.covers: EDB newsletter article introducing the Golden Visa: renewable two-year E-Visa for the investor and immediate family, USD 1 million investment in a qualifying sector within the first 12 months, then eligibility for a Permanent Residence Permit; concierge service.
sources.notes: Page first published 30 Jul 2026, modified 14 Aug 2026 (WordPress metadata).

sources.title: Organic Law Nº 002/2021.OL of 16/07/2021 governing Rwandan nationality, Official Gazette n° Special of 28/07/2021
sources.publisher: Republic of Rwanda (copy published by the Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration)
sources.covers: Art. 15: conditions for Rwandan nationality by acquisition on grounds of substantial sustainable investment or activities; art. 56: in force on publication in the Official Gazette (28 Jul 2021). Kinyarwanda, English and French in parallel columns.
sources.notes: Replaces Organic Law 30/2008, which was not read (so whether an investment ground existed before 2021 is open).

sources.title: Ministerial Order relating to Rwandan nationality, Official Gazette n° Special of 25/03/2022
sources.publisher: Republic of Rwanda, Ministry in charge of immigration (copy published by the Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration)
sources.covers: Art. 12: documents for an application for nationality on grounds of sustainable investment or activities (birth certificate, profile, residence permit, application fee, proof of properties owned, proof of registration as an investor, proof of sustainable activities).
sources.notes: Order number not captured from the extracted text; identified by its gazette date. The application fee amount is not in the article read.

sources.title: Ўзбекистон Республикаси Президентининг Фармони ПФ-67-сон, 18.04.2025: Ишлаб чиқариш, экспорт ва тадбиркорлик фаолиятини рағбатлантириш, савдо ва саноат сиёсати самарадорлигини ошириш чора-тадбирлари тўғрисида (Presidential Decree No. PF-67 of 18 April 2025)
sources.publisher: National Database of Legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan (lex.uz)
sources.covers: Para. 26: from 1 June 2025, a residence permit for 5 years in a simplified procedure for payments of USD 250,000 and USD 150,000 per family member (spouse, child, parent); para. 29: the decree's norms take effect immediately unless a later date is set.
sources.notes: Uzbek (Cyrillic) text, edition shown with change sources dated 18.04.2025 and 10.06.2026 (the stored page is the current consolidated edition, retrieved 2026-10-11). Whether para. 26 was changed on 10.06.2026 was not checked; the 2025 press reports give the same amounts. The implementing procedure (who receives the payment, how to apply) was not found.

sources.title: Узбекистан введёт «золотые визы» для иностранцев с 1 июня
sources.covers: Ministry of Justice announcement of the decree of 18 Apr 2025: five-year residence permit for USD 250,000 plus USD 150,000 per family member, without buying property; updated 1 May 2025 to correct the ministry's first figures (USD 200,000 and 100,000).

sources.title: Стоимость «золотой визы» для иностранцев в Узбекистане составит $250 тысяч, а не $200 тысяч
sources.covers: Correction of the golden-visa price: USD 250,000 and USD 150,000 per family member, as in the presidential decree, not the USD 200,000/100,000 first announced by the Ministry of Justice.
sources.notes: Stored for the record of the corrected announcement; no rows rest on it alone.

program_terms.quote: realizar un aporte directo y no reembolsable al Tesoro Nacional por USD 350.000
program_terms.notes: Announced price; applications to open in Q4 2026; no implementing resolution published yet. valid_from is the announcement date.

program_terms.quote: o suscribir un título público de USD 800.000 creado específicamente para este Programa
program_terms.notes: Announced; bond terms not published.

program_terms.applies_to: spouse; child aged 18-25, single and childless (each)
program_terms.quote: Los cónyuges e hijos de entre 18 y 25 años, solteros y sin hijos, podrán solicitar la ciudadanía mediante un aporte de USD 100.000 al Tesoro Nacional.
Los menores de 18 años podrán hacerlo mediante un aporte de USD 25.000.

program_terms.applies_to: family of four (applicant, spouse, two minor children)
program_terms.quote: un grupo familiar tipo integrado por un solicitante principal, su cónyuge y dos hijos menores, podrá solicitar la ciudadanía argentina por un total de USD 500.000
program_terms.notes: Total of the contributions above, as printed by the ministry.

program_terms.location: In a Nutshell box and para. 6
program_terms.quote: Foreign nationals can now secure a five-year residency ID by purchasing immovable property, provided they invest at least 150,000 dollars.
program_terms.notes: Reported; the text later says the law allows acquisition 'through lease or by investing at least 150,000 dollars', so whether the minimum applies to every purchase is unclear. 'dollars' read as US dollars (the article's fees are in foreign currency; not stated). valid_from: 2026 (in force 24 Feb 2026 per Bantu Gazette).

program_terms.quote: After the purchase is completed, the buyer receives a property-based residential ID valid for up to five years.
program_terms.notes: Revoked if the property is sold.

program_terms.applies_to: property-linked visa up to five years
program_terms.quote: Foreign nationals buying a property can obtain a visa valid for up to five years for the same 4,000 dollar fee.
program_terms.notes: Same fee as the five-year investment visa. Currency stated as 'dollar'; read as USD, not printed.

program_terms.quote: Such circumstances include foreign nationals investing five million dollars and engaging in activities considered favourable to the country's economic development, such as job creation or technology transfer.
program_terms.notes: Reported. Later industry press (Jul 2026, not read) gives USD 10 million. 'dollars' read as US dollars, not printed.

program_terms.quote: Non-Ethiopian nationals seeking it are expected to pay 10,000 dollars.
program_terms.notes: Renewal after 10 years USD 10,000 again; immediate renewal USD 12,500.

program_terms.quote: introduces a Golden Visa, a 10-year multiple-entry permit targeted at investors operating across borders
program_terms.notes: Reported from the Ethiopian Embassy in London's publication.

program_terms.quote: deberán acreditar que forman parte de una o varias figuras mercantiles y/o inviertan en la adquisición de bienes muebles o inmuebles, por un monto de cien mil dólares.
program_terms.notes: Covers shareholdings in companies and purchases of movable or immovable property. 'dólares' read as US dollars; the text says only 'dólares' (unit_basis would be inferred: Guatemala's currency is the quetzal, so the dollar meant is almost certainly the US dollar, but it is not printed). valid_from: 2025, the year of the regulation; its in-force date (set by AMN-05-2025) was not read.

program_terms.applies_to: maximum, temporary residence (1 to 5 years, extendable)
program_terms.quote: Se otorgará la residencia temporal por un periodo de uno a cinco años, según la solicitud planteada por la persona extranjera y lo resuelto por el Instituto Guatemalteco de Migración
Inversionistas: Las personas extranjeras que realicen inversiones en el país, se les autorizará por un plazo no mayor de cinco años.
program_terms.notes: valid_from empty: the Code took effect sixty days after its Diario Oficial publication (date not in the stored copy).

program_terms.applies_to: years of temporary residence before permanent residence
program_terms.quote: Podrán aplicar a la residencia permanente las personas extranjeras que han sido residentes temporales por un periodo igual o mayor de cinco años
program_terms.notes: For former investor residents, dependants can be added on proof that the investment continues.

program_terms.quote: foreign nationals who invest at least $300,000 in the charter capital of Kazakh companies or in publicly traded local securities can apply electronically for the investor visa
program_terms.notes: Press report of the Foreign Ministry announcement; '$' read as US dollars because MyBuh gives 'долларов США'. valid_from is the year only: in force ten days after official publication, date not read.

program_terms.quote: иностранные граждане, инвестировавшие не менее 300 000 долларов США в уставной капитал казахстанских компаний или в местные эмиссионные ценные бумаги, смогут подать электронное ходатайство на оформление инвесторской визы
program_terms.notes: Individuals must show the investment in the 12 months before applying (statement of a securities account with securities of over 10 years' maturity, or a charter-capital increase); legal entities show 36 months of investment documents.

program_terms.quote: Данная «золотая виза» предусматривает возможность последующего получения вида на жительство в РК сроком до 10 лет.
program_terms.notes: Up to 10 years. The petition for the visa is also issued for up to 10 years ('ходатайство выдается сроком до 10 лет').

program_terms.quote: 50 މިލިއަން ޔޫ.އެސް ޑޮލަރު ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގައި އިންވެސްޓް ކޮށްފައިވާ ފަރާތްތައް.
program_terms.notes: 'Persons who have invested 50 million US dollars in the Maldives.' Visa valid for the period of the investment (art. 5(h)1). valid_to assumes the 2021 regulation replaced the 2015 one (not stated).

program_terms.quote: 1 މިލިއަން ޔޫ.އެސް ޑޮލަރު، ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ބޭންކެއްގައި 2 އަހަރު ދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަށް ޑިޕޮސިޓްކޮށްފައިވާ ފަރާތްތައް
program_terms.notes: 'Persons who have deposited 1 million US dollars in a Maldivian bank for 2 years.' Visa valid for 5 years (art. 5(h)2). The same paragraph allows USD 1 million invested in a financial security (separate row).

program_terms.quote: މާލީ މުޤާބިލެއް (މާލީ ސެކިއުރިޓީއެއް) ގައި، 1 މިލިއަން ޔޫ.އެސް ޑޮލަރު އިންވެސްޓްކޮށްފައިވާ ފަރާތްތައް.
program_terms.notes: 'Persons who have invested 1 million US dollars in a financial instrument (financial security).' Visa valid for the period of the investment (art. 5(h)3).

program_terms.quote: ސަރުކާރުގެ ވުޒާރާއަކުން ހުއްދަކުރާ ރިއަލްއެސްޓޭޓްގައި، މަދުވެގެން 1 މިލިއަން ޔޫ.އެސް ޑޮލަރަށް ވުރެ މަދުނުވާ އަދަދަކަށް އިންވެސްޓްކޮށްފައިވާ ފަރާތްތައް.
program_terms.notes: 'Persons who have invested not less than 1 million US dollars in real estate approved by a government ministry.' Visa valid for the term of the title lease (art. 5(h)4).

program_terms.quote: ކޯޕަރޭޓް ރެސިޑެންޓް ވީޒާ ދޫކުރެވޭނީ، އިދާރީ ގޮތުން ޕްރޮސެސިންގ ފީއެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި USD 2000 (ދެހާސް ޔޫ.އެސްޑޮލަރު) ނެގުމަށްފަހުގައެވެ.
program_terms.notes: Administrative processing fee; paid again when the visa is put in a new passport (art. 10(n)).

program_terms.quote: 1 މިލިއަން ޔޫ.އެސް ޑޮލަރު، ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ބޭންކެއްގައި، 2 އަހަރުދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަށް ޑިޕޮސިޓްކޮށްފައިވާ ފަރާތެއްނަމަ، 5 އަހަރު ދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަށް.
program_terms.notes: Other routes: the investment period (USD 50 million and securities) or the title lease (real estate). Renewal every 5 years (art. 5(sh)).

program_terms.applies_to: applicant (family members can also get the visa)
program_terms.quote: ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ބޭންކެއްގައި މަދުވެގެން 250,000 (ދެލައްކަ ފަންސާސް ހާސް) އެމެރިކާ ޑޮލަރު، 5 (ފަހެއް) އަހަރުދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަށް ފިކްސްޑް ޑިޕޮޒިޓް އެކައުންޓެއްގައި ބަހައްޓައިފައިވާކަން
program_terms.notes: 'At least 250,000 US dollars kept in a fixed deposit account in a Maldivian bank for 5 years.' Applicant must be 18 or over (art. 6(h)). The English form (Schedule 1, item 7) reads 'Fixed Deposit US$ 250,000 invested in a licensed bank in the Maldives for a period of 5 years'.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant (family members can also get the visa)
program_terms.quote: ސަރުކާރުން ކަނޑައަޅާ އުސޫލެއްގެ މަތީން، ސަރުކާރުން ކަނޑައަޅާ ވިޔަފާރިތަކުގައި، މަދުވެގެން 250,000 (ދެލައްކަ ފަންސާސް ހާސް) އެމެރިކާ ޑޮލަރު އިންވެސްޓްކޮށް

events.title: Argentina announces citizenship-by-investment prices (USD 350,000 contribution or USD 800,000 bond), applications from Q4 2026
events.description: At Argentina Week in Paris the Minister of Economy and the Chief of Cabinet announced the launch of the programme: USD 350,000 non-refundable contribution to the Treasury or USD 800,000 programme bond, family add-ons, vetting by the Agency with intelligence and financial-intelligence bodies; applications during Q4 2026.

events.description: Reported: the regulation extends the investment entry visa to three and five years and introduces a 10-year Golden Visa; the property-linked visa and residential ID rest on the same regulation (Addis Fortune). Not confirmed from the regulation itself.

programs.notes: Legal basis exists; prices announced on 2 Oct 2026 but the programme was not yet taking applications. Decree of necessity and urgency 366/2025 (28 May 2025) lets foreigners who make a "relevant investment" naturalise regardless of residence and creates the Agencia de Programas de Ciudadanía por Inversión under the Ministry of Economy; Decreto 524/2025 sets the procedure; Ley 27802 (2026) settles tax residence of such citizens; the Agency got an executive director from 22 Apr 2026. The Ministry of Economy has to define what counts as a relevant investment: no such resolution was found in the Boletín Oficial up to 9 Oct 2026 (first section checked day by day from 30 Sep). On 2 Oct 2026 the Minister of Economy announced in Paris that the programme would take applications during the fourth quarter of 2026, with two routes: a non-refundable contribution of USD 350,000 to the National Treasury, or subscription of USD 800,000 in a public bond created for the programme; spouses and children aged 18-25 (single, childless) pay USD 100,000 each and children under 18 USD 25,000 (a family of four: USD 500,000). Applications are vetted by the Agency with SIDE, the UIF and the Security and Interior ministries, and the Dirección Nacional de Migraciones approves or rejects them. Status stays not_operational until applications open; the amounts rest on the ministry's announcement, not yet on a published resolution. Opposition legislators filed a bill to repeal the scheme (Oct 2026, press) and press reports mention court challenges; not researched. Whether Congress has reviewed or rejected the DNU was not checked.

programs.name: Ethiopia property-based residential ID and visa for foreign property buyers
programs.notes: Under the law allowing foreign nationals to acquire immovable property and the revised Immigration & Citizenship Service Fee Regulation (reported as Regulation No. 587/2026, in force 24 Feb 2026 per Bantu Gazette; Addis Fortune says the categories were introduced in February and the regulation was to take effect on publication), a foreigner who buys property in Ethiopia (Addis Fortune: through a lease or an investment of at least USD 150,000) gets a visa valid up to five years (fee USD 4,000) and, after the purchase, a property-based residential ID valid up to five years, both extendable to immediate family; the ID is revoked if the property is sold. The ICS Director General said at a press briefing (spring 2026) that the agency had begun issuing these IDs and visas. Known only from the press: neither the fee regulation nor the property law was found online (the ICS website lists only the 2024 fee regulation 550/2024), so launched and status are left empty. No counts. Ethiopian nationality law has no investor route.

programs.name: Ethiopia Golden Visa (10-year residence and multiple-entry visa for large investors)
programs.notes: A 10-year multiple-entry visa with residence rights, created by the revised Immigration & Citizenship Service Fee Regulation (reported as No. 587/2026, in force 24 Feb 2026). Granted under 'special circumstances', including an investment of USD 5 million in activities that favour development such as job creation or technology transfer (Addis Fortune); fee USD 10,000, renewal USD 10,000 after 10 years or USD 12,500 for immediate renewal. The ICS Director General said in spring 2026 that the agency would 'soon launch these visas'. Industry press in July 2026 (IMI Daily, Business Insider Africa; not read) reports a USD 10 million threshold ahead of a launch later in 2026, which may reflect a later rule or a different reading. Known only from the press; the regulation was not found, so launched and status are empty. No counts.

programs.name: Guatemala temporary residence for investors (residencia temporal para inversionistas, Código de Migración art. 75(d))
programs.notes: The Migration Code (Decreto 44-2016, art. 75(d)) gives foreigners who invest in Guatemala temporary residence for up to five years. The IGM's Reglamento de Residencias Guatemaltecas (Acuerdo IGM-016-2025 of 21 May 2025, approved by the National Migration Authority as AMN-05-2025) requires proof that the applicant is part of one or more commercial entities and/or invests in movable or immovable property for an amount of USD 100,000 ('cien mil dólares'), with a sworn notarial declaration of the activity and planned stay; dependants follow the rules for migrant workers. Temporary residence is granted for one to five years and can be extended; after five years of temporary residence the investor can apply for permanent residence (art. 27). The 2025 regulation repeals Acuerdo IGM-092-2022, which was not read, so whether the USD 100,000 amount is new is unknown and launched is empty; legal_basis is the year of the Migration Code (in force sixty days after its Diario Oficial publication, date not printed in the stored copy). The earlier Ley de Migración (Decreto 95-98) investor category was not researched. Note the route does not require running a business: buying property for USD 100,000 qualifies. No counts of investor residences found (the IGM statistics page was not checked for a residence breakdown). Status left empty.

programs.name: Kazakhstan investor visa ('golden visa', инвесторская виза) with residence permit of up to 10 years
programs.notes: A foreigner who has invested the equivalent of at least USD 300,000 in the charter capital of a Kazakh company or in local listed securities (with a maturity of over 10 years, per MyBuh) within the 12 months before applying gets a petition for an investor visa valid for up to 10 years and can then obtain a residence permit for up to 10 years. Created by amendments to the Rules for issuing a petition for an investor visa (Order No. 1265 of the Minister for Investment and Development, 29 Dec 2015), approved on 30 April 2025 per the Foreign Ministry and in force ten days after official publication; the amending order and its in-force date were not read (adilet.zan.kz and gov.kz could not be fetched), so launched is empty. The 2015 investor visa itself predates the USD 300,000 threshold; whether it had a stated minimum was not checked. Press reports in August 2026 say the President asked Parliament to pass a law on the 'golden visa' and a new migration law quickly; not followed. Ordinary naturalisation in Kazakhstan requires 5 years' permanent residence; no investor route to citizenship found. No counts found (a 2025 headline asks how many investor applications were approved; not read).

programs.name: Maldives Corporate Resident Visa (ކޯޕަރޭޓް ރެސިޑެންޓް ވީޒާ) for investors
programs.notes: A long-stay residence visa for foreigners who invest in the Maldives, issued under the Immigration Act (Law 1/2007). First set up by Regulation 2015/R-139 (in force on its gazette publication, 27 Apr 2015, art. 13): investors of USD 50 million in the Maldives, of USD 1 million deposited in a Maldivian bank for 2 years or put in a financial security, or of at least USD 1 million in real estate approved by a ministry, with spouse and children under 18, and for companies a limited number of directors and executives; USD 2,000 processing fee; the visa ran for the investment period, 5 years, or the title lease. Reformed by Regulation 2021/R-115 (in force on gazette publication, 29 Aug 2021, art. 22), run by the Registrar of Businesses: a USD 250,000 fixed deposit in a Maldivian bank for 5 years, or USD 250,000 invested in businesses the government designates, gives a 5-year renewable visa for the applicant and family (parents, spouse, children, grandparents, grandchildren); fee MVR 750 per three months (MVR 15,000 in total). The 2021 regulation also covers shareholders, directors and top-five managers of a registered foreign investment that employs at least 50% Maldivians and had USD 1 million revenue in one of the last three years; that branch rests on the company's figures, not a personal investment, so it is out of scope under decision 15 and is not recorded as a price. The 2021 text does not say it repeals the 2015 regulation; the 2015 amounts are recorded until 28 Aug 2021 on the assumption that the 2021 regulation replaced them, which no document read states. Art. 21 of the 2021 regulation requires the ministry to publish every quarter the number of visas issued and the nationalities on business.egov.mv; no such figures were found. Residence on this visa does not lead to citizenship (Maldivian citizenship is not available by naturalisation to non-Muslims; no investor route found). A separate 'Pearl Residence' programme announced with Henley & Partners in July 2025 is reported only by the press and was not found in the gazette. Status left empty: no official statement found on whether the visa is issued today.

programs.name: Mauritius Golden Visa Scheme (USD 1 million investment, path to permanent residence)
programs.notes: Announced in the 2026/27 Budget and run by the Economic Development Board with the Passport and Immigration Office. The applicant signs an undertaking to invest at least USD 1 million in a qualifying sector (financial services, fintech, ICT, tourism, manufacturing, healthcare, education, renewable energy, blue economy, creative and knowledge-based industries) within 12 months of the visa being issued, and shows a bank balance of USD 1 million; he and his spouse and children get a multi-entry visa valid up to two years, renewable, with no processing fee and a five-working-day target. Once the USD 1 million is invested in a qualifying business activity within the 12 months, the holder can apply for a Permanent Residence Permit; failure can lead to cancellation or non-renewal. Holders may buy residential property under the IRS, RES, PDS and Smart City schemes. launched is the month of the EDB guidelines (August 2026), the earliest official operating text found; no regulation or Finance Act provision is cited, and the press (Bloomberg, Fortune, May 2026) reported the plan, including a target of 100 investors a year, which was not found in an official text. Status active: the EDB guidelines describe the application process as open on NELS. No counts. Separate from the older investor occupation permit and property-purchase residence (mus-investor-permit, mus-property-residence).

programs.name: Rwanda nationality by acquisition on grounds of substantial sustainable investment (Organic Law 002/2021.OL, art. 15)
programs.notes: A foreigner may apply for Rwandan nationality by acquisition on grounds of 'substantial sustainable investment or activities' in Rwanda, supported by a letter from a relevant public body describing the investment, plus integrity and no threat to national security (Organic Law 002/2021.OL of 16 Jul 2021, art. 15, in force on publication 28 Jul 2021). The 2022 ministerial order (art. 12) asks for proof of properties owned and of registration as an investor in Rwanda. No minimum amount, price or fee schedule is set in the texts read, so the route is discretionary; launched is the law's in-force date, as the first text found that names investment as a ground (the 2008 law it replaced was not read). Separate investor residence permits exist (permit class A1 'investor' under the immigration ministerial order, defined by reference to the investment law); they were not added because no amount was found in the immigration texts. No counts of nationality grants on this ground found. Status left empty: no document says whether anyone has been naturalised this way.

programs.name: Uzbekistan 'golden visa': five-year residence permit for a USD 250,000 payment (Presidential Decree PF-67 of 18 April 2025, para. 26)
programs.notes: From 1 June 2025 foreign citizens and stateless persons can get a five-year Uzbek residence permit (яшаш гувоҳномаси, вид на жительство) in a simplified procedure in return for payments of USD 250,000 for the applicant and USD 150,000 for each family member (spouse, child, parent), without buying property (Presidential Decree PF-67 of 18 April 2025, para. 26). launched is 1 June 2025, the date para. 26 itself sets; the decree took effect on signature/publication (para. 29). The Ministry of Justice first announced USD 200,000 and USD 100,000 and corrected this to the decree's amounts (Gazeta.uz, 1 May 2025). Who receives the payment and the application procedure were not found; whether the payment is refundable is not stated in para. 26 (read as a non-refundable payment, тўлов). A 10-year 'Golden visa' for large investors was already announced as a plan in Resolution PP-3836 of 4 July 2018 but no rules were found. Separate from the property-purchase residence permit of Decree UP-5611 (uzb-property-residence). No counts found.

Decree UP-5611 (in force 06.01.2019) gives citizens of the countries listed in its Annex 6 the right to a residence permit on purchase of real estate worth at least USD 400,000 in Tashkent city and region, USD 200,000 in Samarkand, Bukhara, Namangan, Andijan, Fergana and Khorezm regions, and USD 100,000 in Karakalpakstan and other regions. Decree UP-101 of 8 April 2022 cut the Tashkent threshold to USD 300,000. The 2025 'golden visa' (USD 250,000 payment, no property needed) is recorded separately as uzb-golden-visa (Decree PF-67 of 18 Apr 2025, para. 26). A 2019 investor residence rule was not confirmed from primary texts. No official counts found.

gaps: Argentina: no Ministry of Economy resolution defining the 'relevant investment' (amounts, bond terms) in the Boletín Oficial up to 9 Oct 2026; opposition repeal bill (Carignano, 9 Oct 2026) and reported court challenges (Chequeado, 9 Oct 2026) not researched.

Ethiopia: the Immigration & Citizenship Service Fee Regulation (reported No. 587/2026) and the proclamation allowing foreigners to own residential property were not found online (Negarit Gazette not reachable; the ICS website, searched through its WordPress search in English and Amharic, lists only Regulation 550/2024); the USD 5 million (Addis Fortune) versus USD 10 million (IMI Daily, Business Insider Africa, Jul 2026; not read) Golden Visa threshold is unresolved; no counts.

Guatemala: the in-force date of the residence regulation (AMN-05-2025 approval), the repealed Acuerdo IGM-092-2022 (whether it already had a USD 100,000 investor requirement) and the earlier Ley de Migración 95-98 investor category were not read; no counts of investor residences found; residence fees (Reglamento de Tarifas, IGM-029-2023 as amended, linked on the IGM legislation page) not extracted.

Kazakhstan investor visa: the amending order to Order No. 1265 (29 Dec 2015), its number, publication and in-force dates, and the 2015 order's original conditions were not read: adilet.zan.kz's document API now requires credentials (not attempted further) and gov.kz/egov.kz pages are script-rendered. No counts of investor visas or residence permits found. The 2026 'golden visa' bill (reported Aug 2026) and new migration law not followed.

Maldives Corporate Resident Visa: no count of visas issued found, although art. 21 of Regulation 2021/R-115 requires quarterly publication on business.egov.mv (not reachable as a public statistics page); no gazetted list of 'government-designated businesses' for the USD 250,000 investment route; whether the 2015 regulation was formally repealed is not stated in the 2021 text.

Maldives 'Pearl Residence' programme (Henley & Partners agreement reported 1 Jul 2025; press items Jul 2025-Sep 2026 on investor visa/residency and a Rasmalé link): no regulation, law or official announcement found in the Maldives gazette (title search for residency, visa, immigration and investment terms in Dhivehi, laws and regulations) or the President's Office site; not added. The Immigration Act's latest amendment (Law 3/2025, stored) is unrelated. Edition.mv articles were not read because the site blocks AI crawlers.

Note on method: the session's web-search allowance was exhausted at the start of this pass, so candidates were checked through Google News RSS listings and official sites fetched directly; absence of a programme below is less certain than usual.

Mauritius Golden Visa: the legal instrument (Finance Act 2026 or immigration regulations) and the Budget 2026/27 speech paragraph were not read; the press-reported cap or target of 100 investors a year (Bloomberg 5 May 2026) was not found officially; no counts.

Rwanda: no count of nationality grants on investment grounds; Organic Law 30/2008 (predecessor) not read; investor residence permits (class A1, ministerial order relating to immigration, migration.gov.rw) carry no stated amount in the order read, and the investment-law registration threshold was not checked, so no residence programme was added.

Uzbekistan golden visa: implementing procedure (recipient of the payment, application route, refundability), the 10.06.2026 amendment of Decree PF-67 (whether it touched para. 26) and any counts were not found. The 2018 plan for a 10-year 'Golden visa' for large investors (Resolution PP-3836 of 4 Jul 2018, lex.uz/ru/docs/3810645) produced no rules found.

Botswana: not added. Parliament passed the Citizenship (Amendment) Bill 2025 on 17 Dec 2025 (stored: bwa-dailynews-parliament-2025), and the Parliament bills page lists the consequential National Registration (Amendment) Bill No. 35 of 2025 as 'Passed' (entries dated 12 Dec 2025 and 23 Apr 2026; https://www.parliament.gov.bw/index.php?option=com_parliament&view=bills&Itemid=944, searched for 'citizenship' on 2026-10-11). The Citizenship (Amendment) Bill/Act itself is not on that page; no assent, gazetted Act, commencement or regulations found, and Google News listings of Aug 2026 (Wansom AI, 24 and 26 Aug 2026, not read) report the 'Impact Citizenship' programme stalled pending regulations. Price (USD 75,000-100,000) only in industry and press reports.

Ghana: not added. The Ghana Investment Promotion Authority Bill 2026 (stored: gha-parl-gipa-bill-2026) only directs the Interior Ministry to legislate on citizenship by investment (clause 39); IMI Daily 9 Jun 2026 ('Ghana's Investment Bill Introduces Citizenship by Investment in a Single Clause', not read) confirms it is a single enabling clause. No programme, price or regulations.

Nigeria: not added. Only a constitution alteration bill (House bill HB 2059, second reading reported Mar 2025; NALTF page 30 Jul 2025 'Nigeria Moves Towards Investment-Focused Citizenship', https://naltf.gov.ng, not read) - not enacted.

Namibia: not added. The Ministry of Home Affairs said in 2023-25 it was drafting a golden visa (lead: https://nbcnews.na/node/100236); no law or regulation found; the reported NAD 2 million investor visa and President's Links Estate route appear only in industry material.

Kenya: out of scope. The Class G permit (specific trade, business or consultancy) in the Kenya Citizenship and Immigration Regulations 2012 (LN 64/2012, consolidated 30 May 2025, https://new.kenyalaw.org/akn/ke/act/ln/2012/64/eng@2025-05-30) requires 'sufficient capital and other resources for the purpose' with no stated minimum; the USD 100,000 figure in secondary sources is not in the regulations. Decision 15: business permit without a set investment amount.

Uganda: not added. Class G investor permit with a reported USD 250,000 minimum; ULII (Uganda Citizenship and Immigration Control Act) returned 403 to scripts and ugandainvest.go.ug is script-rendered, so no official amount was read.

Tanzania: not added. Class A residence permit for investors rests on a Tanzania Investment Centre certificate, whose threshold (reported USD 300,000-500,000) is the project's capital, not the applicant's own investment (decision 15: company capital thresholds are out); Immigration Act Cap. 54 and Investment Act 2022 not read (tanzlii not tried).

Rwanda: investor residence permit (class A1) not added - no amount in the immigration ministerial order (migration.gov.rw/laws); the investment-ground naturalisation was added (rwa-investor-naturalisation).

Egypt residence for property owners: not added. Press items (Youm7 15 Dec 2018 on Interior Ministry decisions on residence of foreign property owners; Safha1 9 Oct 2025 '5 years' residence for USD 200,000') point to Interior Ministry decrees that were not found in an official copy (youm7 site search failed; MOI site not tried). Worth a dedicated pass: a property-purchase residence route would be in scope.

Mozambique: not added. Decreto 46/2022 (16 Sep 2022, amending arts. 17, 18, 21 of the foreigners regulation) reportedly gives 2- and 5-year residence for investment projects of USD 500,000 and USD 50 million (project size, likely company-level); Boletim da República text not found.

Angola, Madagascar, Morocco, Tunisia, Senegal, Guinea-Bissau, Djibouti, Seychelles (new routes), Comoros (relaunch): nothing found beyond the earlier pass (research-cbi-new-countries-clean): Angola's investor visa and Madagascar's investor visa have no stated minimum; Google News checks on 2026-10-11 found no new programme for Morocco, Tunisia, Senegal, Guinea-Bissau, Djibouti or a Comoros relaunch (only the Kiwan ICSID arbitration, Apr 2025). Absence not proven.

Kyrgyzstan: not added. Investor visas (reported KGS 10 million / 20 million, amendments to the Law on External Migration in force March 2023) could not be read: cbd.minjust.gov.kg serves a reCAPTCHA-protected script page; Azattyk (12 Jan 2023) is the only dated report seen.

Japan: out of scope. The Business Manager residence status rests on the company's capital (¥5 million, raised to ¥30 million in 2025 per press) and running the business, not a personal investment (decision 15 refined; the earlier pass dropped it for the same reason).

Singapore, Sri Lanka: existing rows checked for news only; no new route found (Sri Lanka 'My Dream Home' visa is deposit-plus-income for retirees, not checked against an official text; the Golden Paradise increase from US$100,000 to US$200,000 remains undated).
Solomon Islands: not added. A citizenship-by-investment bill was drafted (ABC 3 Nov 2024) but RNZ reported on 28 Apr 2025 that it had 'still a long way to go'; no Act found.

Kiribati (1990s investor passports), Tuvalu (passport sales from 1997), Palau, Cook Islands, Niue: not added. Kiribati and Tuvalu schemes are known only from academic mentions (EUI report); no official texts read. No investment route found for Palau, Cook Islands or Niue (news checks; the 2026 US Investment Climate Statement for Palau was not read).

The temporary-residence subcategory 'Inversionistas' (https://serviciomigraciones.cl/residencia-temporal/subcategorias/inversionistas/) is for legal representatives and managers of a foreign company that invests at least USD 500,000: the investment is the company's (decision 15: company money thresholds are out). Not stored.

Belize: not added. A USD 500,000 investor fast-track to permanent residence was proposed in Dec 2025 (IMI Daily 19 Dec 2025) and was still described as a proposal in Oct 2026 (CEOWORLD 11 Oct 2026); no law found. The old economic citizenship programme (blz-ecp) is unchanged.

Jamaica: not added. Investor residency bills were moving toward Parliament (Jamaica Observer 29 Jul 2026; IMI Daily 4 Aug 2026) and a 'golden passport' plan was reported (Gleaner 3 Oct 2026); nothing enacted found.

Investor and shareholder residence through DIMAS (industry sites cite Afl. 125,000-250,000 shareholdings, USD 200,000 property) could not be confirmed: dimas.aw did not respond and the gobierno.aw pages read (work and residence permit, DIMAS) only refer to the Landsverordening toelating en uitzetting without amounts.

Trinidad and Tobago press (Jul 2026) discusses others' CBI programmes only.

Puerto Rico: out of scope. Act 60 (individual resident investor decree) is a tax regime for people who become residents; it grants no immigration residence (residence in Puerto Rico is governed by US immigration law), so no investment buys residence. Note for consistency: che-lump-sum-taxation and ury-tax-residence-investment are in the data; whether Act 60 should be treated like them is a judgement for a person.
